In an extensive interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman responded to the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and discussed their plans for a tab-less interface. Watch the video below.

Work functionality will likely soon be seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT

A few days ago, Joanna Stern posted a teaser clip of her interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her new YouTube channel, New Things.

Today, Stern published the full interview, covering a range of topics including the new ChatGPT Voice, OpenAI's hardware ambitions, the lawsuit against Apple, and the recent Hugging Face breach.

During the conversation, Stern brought up OpenAI's recent decision to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps, along with the launch of the new agentic Work mode for ChatGPT.

The result was a confusing interface, especially for users who just wanted to keep using ChatGPT and couldn't for the life of them find their chat history.

OpenAI later updated the app, adding back separate Work and Chat tabs at the top and a dropdown in the sidebar for switching between ChatGPT and Codex. While the app is less unwieldy than before, it still feels roundabout to use.

When asked about the misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern that the new interface was "a bit of a mess," but added that this was a "stepping stone to the future," noting that the Work tab will eventually go away and its functionality will be "seamlessly woven into ChatGPT."

Here's Brockman's full response:

Brockman also said that while the rollout of the merged app was confusing, OpenAI is already seeing the intended effect: Codex users doubled from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When Stern pressed on whether that growth was simply the result of forcing Codex into the ChatGPT app, Brockman again conceded that was the case, while also arguing that this was partly the point:

The full interview is quite interesting and well worth watching. It even includes a very Joanna Stern-style attempt to bring ChatGPT Voice into the conversation, and the results are about what you'd expect.
